title: Novus Search — Embeddings & Reranking Discovery
summary: Discovery call to understand Novus Search's current vector search setup, throughput requirements, dimensionality decisions, and options between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for embeddings + rerank pipeline. Agreement to run a small POC benchmark and share pricing + security docs.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated sizing guide
Redwood SE to share security docs (SOC 2, ISO, network architecture) and sample config for VPC private deployment
Schedule 2-week POC: benchmark 100k docs with hybrid retrieval + reranker
Novus to provide sample dataset and expected QPS/latency targets
action_items: Alex Chen — Send tailored pricing & Dedicated sizing (due: 2027-04-01)
Rashmi Patel — Share security pack + recommended architecture diagram for VPC (due: 2027-03-30)
Daniel Kim — Provide sample subset of 100k docs and current index stats (due: 2027-03-29)
Priya Rao — Confirm stakeholders for POC and preferred test queries (due: 2027-03-29)
transcript: [00:00] Alex Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intro, i'm alex with redwood — i'm the account lead. rashmi from our se team will run the technic stuff — rashmi?
[00:08] Rashmi Patel: hey all, rashmi here. excited to dig into your embeddings + rerank flow and latency goals.

[00:15] Daniel Kim: thanks alex, priya and jorge here too. we run Novus Search — mainly e-commerce search, lots of short queries and product documents. current infra is elastic + a small faiss cluster.
[00:30] Priya Rao: yes, our main ask is better semantic recall and reranking; we see some cold-start problems and re-ranking latency spikes during peak.
[00:40] Rashmi Patel: got it. quick clarifying q: are you storing embeddings in your vector DB (faiss) or using redwood to serve nearest neighbor/rerank calls?

[00:50] Jorge Mendes: today we generate embeddings in-house using open models and push to FAISS. we do a hybrid where elastic does bm25 first then we use faiss for semantic, then a small cross-encoder re-ranker but it's pretty slow and expensive.

[01:05] Alex Chen: good context. two main patterns customers use with redwood: 1) hosted embeddings + rerank API (we compute embeddings and return vectors or reranked doc ids), or 2) you keep a vector DB and call redwood for on-demand reranking/cross-encoder scoring. both have tradeoffs.
[01:22] Daniel Kim: what's the throughput like for reranking at redwood? we need to support ~200 QPS at peak with 100 candidates per query ideally.

[01:30] Rashmi Patel: for hosted endpoints, with dedicated capacity we can guarantee throughput to hit 200 QPS for 100-candidate reranks — you'd likely want dedicated pools sized for your peak. hosted multi-tenant can scale too but not SLA'd. for private/VPC deployments we can push the capacity onto your network and meet the same numbers with dedicated GPUs.
[01:48] Priya Rao: and embedding dimensionality — we're currently using 1536 dims from an older model. is there benefit moving to 1024 or 768? storage/cost is a concern.

[01:58] Rashmi Patel: tradeoffs: lower dims reduce storage and NN speed, sometimes slight recall drop. recommend evaluating 1536 vs 1024 with your workload; some models with 1024 give similar quality for short product queries. we can run A/B in the POC.
[02:12] Jorge Mendes: we also use hnsw with faiss — any gotchas integrating with redwood? latency on our side is okay but we want the reranker to be fast.

[02:20] Rashmi Patel: integration options: you keep hnsw/faiss as the vector store and call it as usual; then send top-k ids+contexts to redwood for rerank. or, you can store embeddings in our managed index and call a single rerank endpoint. keeping your own vector DB gives more control over consistency and local tuning; using Redwood managed index simplifies operations and gives combined metrics in the console.

[02:40] Alex Chen: operationally customers choose dedicated when they need predictable latency/cost and private if they need VPC/KMS and full control. hosted is fastest to get started — generate embeddings via our API and push them to your store or ours.
[02:55] Priya Rao: security: we need SOC 2 type II, SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs. also data residency in us-east. can redwood support that in hosted?

[03:07] Rashmi Patel: hosted customers get SOC 2; for dedicated we can offer stricter tenancy and contracts. for KMS and VPC, that's typically Private deployment or a Dedicated setup with VPC peering depending on the account. we'll share the security pack with specifics.
[03:22] Daniel Kim: about reranker architecture — we've been using a cross-encoder late-stage re-ranker that's too slow. what models/patterns does redwood recommend for fast rerank?

[03:32] Rashmi Patel: two patterns: 1) use a bi-encoder for fast dot-product scoring for initial semantic ranking (cheap), followed by 2) a lightweight cross-encoder LLM only on top N (e.g., top 10) for final re-ordering. Redwood supports both: fast embedding scoring on dedicated hardware and low-latency cross-encoder on GPU with batching.
[03:50] Priya Rao: batching: how does that affect latency? we can't add too much tail latency for interactive search.

[03:58] Rashmi Patel: batching helps throughput and reduces cost but increases tail latency. with Dedicated you can configure batch windows and autoscaling policies. Redwood's smart routing picks policies to respect latency SLOs while still batching where helpful.
[04:15] Jorge Mendes: any specifics on approximate NN — does redwood have its own index we can use? we wanted to avoid re-building indexes if possible.

[04:23] Rashmi Patel: Redwood doesn't force you onto our index; we integrate with common vector DBs. If you want to migrate, we have tooling to export/import embeddings. For POC it's simplest to keep your FAISS and call Redwood for rerank to measure improvements without a full reindex.
[04:40] Alex Chen: curious about cost: do you have guidance for cost per QPS for a 100-candidate rerank pipeline at 200 QPS?

[04:48] Rashmi Patel: rough back-of-envelope: bi-encoder dot products are cheap if using embeddings only. The expensive part is cross-encoder LLM compute. With Dedicated, you amortize the GPU cost; we'll send a sizing guide — we'll propose a cluster config that hits 200 QPS with top-100 candidate scoring and top-10 cross-encoder. exact cost depends on embedding model and batching windows.
[05:10] Daniel Kim: models — do you recommend any embedding models? we tested text-embedding-3-small and some open-weights locally.

[05:18] Rashmi Patel: we recommend starting with a high-quality open model we verify in our catalog (we'll share perf profiles). text-embedding-3-classic (example) or comparable 1536-dim models are good. for small product queries, 1024-dim variants often work; we'll validate quality trade-offs in the POC.
[05:35] Priya Rao: about hybrid search: we're currently doing bm25+semantic. is it better to do a pre-filter with bm25 then do faiss then rerank?

[05:43] Rashmi Patel: that's a common and effective pattern: lexical retrieval to catch exact matches and boost precision, then semantic retrieval to expand recall, then rerank. Redwood's console can show token-level cost and per-route latency so you can tune which step runs where.
[05:58] Jorge Mendes: any notes about dimensionality and quantization? we need to store 10M vectors, so storage matters.

[06:06] Rashmi Patel: options: quantize your vector DB (e.g., IVF+PQ) to save space; some open vector DBs and FAISS support PQ. If you use Redwood managed index we support lower-bit quantization profiles and will recommend settings. quantization can slightly affect recall — part of POC to measure.
[06:22] Alex Chen: just to surface typical enterprise questions — SLA uptime, data retention policies, contract terms; Priya is that something your legal/procurement will review upfront?
[06:32] Priya Rao: yes, we'll need that for procurement. also need IP/data handling clauses and a runbook for incident response.
[06:40] Rashmi Patel: we'll include the legal/security pack and an example runbook. for Private deployments we can do on-prem or VPC with customer-managed KMS for keys.
[06:52] Daniel Kim: for the POC, timeline wise we want something in 2–3 weeks. what do you need from us?

[07:00] Alex Chen: ideal: you send a 100k doc sample and representative queries; we'll run a POC for 2 weeks measuring recall and latency. we'll produce a benchmark sheet and propose Dedicated sizing.
[07:12] Priya Rao: ok i'll coordinate that — also confirm stakeholders for decision making post-POC.
[07:18] Rashmi Patel: quick note on metrics we'll track: recall@10, MRR, avg/95th latency, cost per 1k queries, and memory/drive usage for indexes.
[07:28] Jorge Mendes: sounds good. curious: can redwood's reranker operate within our VPC to avoid hitting the public internet?

[07:35] Rashmi Patel: yes — Private deployment supports VPC peering or on-prem connectors. Dedicated can also be placed in a private network in some cloud regions; we'll map options in the security doc.
[07:46] Alex Chen: any blockers that would make us recommend Private outright?

[07:50] Rashmi Patel: if you have strict data residency, customer-managed KMS, or regulatory requirements that prohibit managed multi-tenant endpoints, Private or on-prem is the right path. otherwise Dedicated gives similar performance with simpler ops.
[08:02] Daniel Kim: about monitoring — do you provide per-route dashboards and logs?
[08:07] Rashmi Patel: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route latency, token and compute breakdowns, trace hooks, and error analysis. we can also export logs to your Splunk/Datadog.
[08:18] Priya Rao: we use DataDog and want to ingest cost/latency metrics — great to hear.
[08:24] Alex Chen: ok i'll summarize next steps: send pricing and Dedicated sizing, SE share security docs and architecture, schedule the POC, and we run benchmarks. anything else?
[08:33] Daniel Kim: can you include a sample config for hybrid retrieval + rerank? that would help our infra team.
[08:38] Rashmi Patel: yes — i'll include diagram and an example pipeline config (bm25 -> faiss top-k -> bi-encoder -> cross-encoder top10).
[08:46] Priya Rao: timeline: once we get docs we'll try to turn POC around in two weeks — procurement may take longer but we'll try to align.
[08:54] Alex Chen: great. any competitors we should know about you're evaluating?
[08:58] Daniel Kim: team looked at pinecone and weaviate plus some managed elastic offerings.
[09:04] Rashmi Patel: noted — we'll include comparison notes in the sendover.
[09:10] Alex Chen: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the items discussed. wrap up?
[09:15] Priya Rao: that's it from me, thanks.
[09:18] Jorge Mendes: thanks, bye.
[09:21] Daniel Kim: thanks, bye.
[09:25] Alex Chen: bye all, we'll shoot the email after the call.
